newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan oil, gas demand said rising six pct/year.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan oil, gas demand said rising six pct/year.

text.p: Pakistan's oil and gas demand is rising at six percent a a year and the sector provides good investment opportunities, an oil company executive said on Monday.
"Oil and gas demand is growing at about six percent per annum," Tom Higgins, chief executive of Shell Pakistan Ltd, told a seminar for visiting British businessmen.
He said demand for oil products was expected to reach 29.5 million tonnes by 2005, from 15.9 million in 1995/96 (July-June).

"From exploration and production upstream to refining and downstream marketing (including infrastructure projects), there is already active interest by a large number of players from Europe, North America and the Far East," he said.
Government strategy and policies were designed to meet the twin objectives of limiting the import bill and reducing dependence on imports for national security reasons, he said.
"Never has there been a better time to invest in Pakistan and in particular in the oil and gas sector," Higgins said.

He said Pakistan currently produces about 25 percent of its crude oil requirement and refines about 35 percent of its petroleum needs. Imports of oil and products are expected to cost about $2 billion in fiscal 1996/97.
Shell Pakistan Ltd is 51 percent owned by the Royal Dutch Petroleum Co.

The Lord Mayor of London, Alderman Roger Cork, told the seminar British investment in Pakistan had risen to $317 million in 1995/96 from $82 million in 1992/93, with the oil and gas sector accounting for a substantial proportion.
He said two-way trade between Britain and Pakistan had exceeded $1 billion in calendar 1995. Britain was the second largest foreign investor in Pakistan after the United States.
